content.text: {"answers":[{"id":"p1","answer":"The documentation doesn't settle this. It only records that `total` is a constructor parameter with default `None` (\"Total expected iterations\") and that all such initialisation happens in `tqdm.__init__` [tqdm/std.py:355-635]. The wiki pages given never describe the fallback of inferring `total` from `len(iterable)`, so I can't confirm from the docs that `self.total` becomes 4 for `tqdm(chars)` with a 4-element list — only that, absent any inference, the documented default is `None`. (Indirect hints exist: the `tqdm.contrib.itertools`/`tenumerate` wrappers explicitly compute a `total` because the underlying iterators have no length, which implies std tqdm uses the iterable's length when one exists, but that is inference, not documentation.)"},{"id":"p2","answer":"The documentation does not describe `update` being called with batched `n` values from `__iter__`. What it does document is: `update(n=1)` advances the bar by `n` [tqdm/std.py:879-915], and that display refreshes are throttled by `mininterval` (default 0.1 s) and `miniters`, with `miniters` dynamically adjusted when left as `None`/0 [tqdm/std.py:353-368]. With 0.05 s sleeps and a 0.1 s `mininterval`, the throttling naturally groups two iterations per refresh, which is consistent with two refreshes each covering 2 items — but the claim that `tqdm.update` itself is invoked twice with `n=2` (rather than four times with `n=1` and two of them triggering a redraw) is not something the provided documentation establishes."},{"id":"p3","answer":"Not settled by the documentation. The docs say `close()` \"closes the progress bar and cleans up resources\" [tqdm/std.py:1266-1307] and that the displayed rate is normally smoothed with an exponential moving average (`EMA`, `smoothing` default 0.3) [tqdm/std.py:214-242], and that `format_dict` is the dictionary of formatting values that subclasses can extend [tqdm/std.py:1465-1481]. They do not state that `close()` disables smoothing or that `format_dict['rate']` afterwards becomes the plain overall average `n/elapsed`, so I can't confirm the exact reason for the 17.50 → 17.39 it/s difference from what is documented."},{"id":"p4","answer":"The documentation describes `close()` as the method that closes the bar and cleans up resources, and it recommends either a `with` block (which calls `close()` automatically) or an explicit `close()`/`del` when not using one [README.rst:196-220], [tqdm/std.py:1266-1307]. It does not document the behaviour of calling `close()` twice (idempotency / early return on an already-closed bar), so I can't say from the docs what the second call from `__del__` does beyond the fact that the recommended pattern treats both paths as equivalent cleanup."},{"id":"p5","answer":"The provided documentation doesn't cover `_get_free_pos`. It documents only that `position` is a parameter (\"Position for multiple bars\", default `None`) [tqdm/std.py:246-359] and that live bars are tracked in the class-level `WeakSet` `tqdm._instances` [tqdm/std.py:254]. The natural reading is that position is allocated from the set of currently-live instances, so if the first bar was already closed (and hence removed from `_instances`) before the second was created, slot 0 is free again — but the allocation rule itself is not documented here, so treat that as inference."},{"id":"p6","answer":"I can't reproduce it verbatim from the documentation. The docs describe the layout as `{l_bar}{bar}{r_bar}` where `l_bar` is description + percentage [tqdm/std.py:596], `bar` is rendered by `Bar.__format__` [tqdm/std.py:603], [tqdm/std.py:183-209], and `r_bar` holds counts, timing and rate [tqdm/std.py:598]; `Bar` fills a width (derived from `ncols`/`dynamic_ncols`) with UTF-8 block characters (or ASCII if `ascii` is set), using partial blocks for the fractional part [tqdm/std.py:142-149]. So the shape is `Processing b:  50%|<half-filled bar>| 2/4 [00:00<00:00, 18.13it/s]`, but the exact number of block characters depends on the terminal width/`ncols` at runtime, which the documentation does not fix."},{"id":"p7","answer":"The documentation supports the general path: the constructor finishes by rendering the bar, i.e. `tqdm.__init__` → `refresh()`/`display()` → `format_meter()` → write to `file` (default `sys.stderr`) [tqdm/std.py:355-635], [tqdm/std.py:1335-1354], [tqdm/std.py:465-661]. The `?` placeholders appear because with `n=0` and essentially zero elapsed time no rate can be computed, so no ETA can be derived either; the docs confirm `?it/s` is a real rendered form (the nbval regex normalises `[?\\s\\d.]+(it/s|s/it)` → `?it/s` and `00:0[01]<(00:0[01]|\\?)` → `00:00<00:00` [.meta/nbval.ini:1-6]), but they don't spell out the exact branch in `format_meter` that substitutes `?`."},{"id":"p8","answer":"The documentation states that the `tqdm` class \"creates if needed\" a single `TMonitor` background thread [tqdm/_monitor.py:16-40], that it is a daemon named `tqdm_monitor` driven by `sleep_interval` (from `monitor_interval`, default 10 s), and that it is shut down via `was_killed`/`_atexit_signal()`/`exit()` [tqdm/_monitor.py:31-54]. So the second bar reuses the already-running monitor rather than spawning another; `report()` is the liveness check (it reports whether the thread is still running), and a new monitor would be started when no live monitor exists — e.g. after the previous one was killed/exited, or when the monitoring configuration changes. The exact condition inside `tqdm.__new__` is not reproduced in the documentation."},{"id":"g1","answer":"The docs only give the coarse rule: `leave` defaults to `True` and means \"Keep progress bar after completion\" [tqdm/std.py:246-359], [tqdm/tqdm.1:52-57]; with `leave=False` the finished bar is removed — this is visible in the specialised implementations too (e.g. `tqdm_gui.close()` closes the figure when `leave` is False [tqdm/gui.py:105], and `tqdm_telegram`/`tqdm_discord` `close()` delete the message when the bar isn't meant to stay [tqdm/contrib/telegram.py:137-143], [tqdm/contrib/discord.py:140-145]). The semantics of `leave=None` are not documented in the material provided."},{"id":"g2","answer":"The documentation only says `disable` (default `False`) \"Disable the entire progress bar\" [tqdm/std.py:246-359], [tqdm/tqdm.1]. It does not enumerate what remains usable on a disabled instance (e.g. whether `update()`, `close()`, `set_description()` or `format_dict` still work). One related documented mechanism is `DisableOnWriteError`, which disables a bar on stream failure by setting `miniters` to `inf` [tqdm/utils.py:166-204], implying disabling is implemented by suppressing output rather than by breaking the API — but that is the wrapper's behaviour, not a documented guarantee for `disable=True`."},{"id":"g3","answer":"`TMonitor` is a background daemon thread that guarantees each active bar is refreshed at least once per its `maxinterval`, so a bar doesn't look frozen during slow iterations [tqdm/_monitor.py:16-20]. Each cycle it waits `sleep_interval` (from `monitor_interval`, default 10 s), takes `tqdm_cls.get_lock()`, copies the started instances from `_instances`, and for any instance where `miniters > 1` and `now - last_print_t >= maxinterval` it sets `miniters = 1` and calls `refresh(nolock=True)` [tqdm/_monitor.py:56-93]. Shutdown is via `was_killed` (`_atexit_signal()` at interpreter exit, or `exit()` which also joins) [tqdm/_monitor.py:39-54]. The documentation shows `monitor_interval` as the knob (tests set `tqdm.monitor_interval`) but does not explicitly state that setting it to 0 disables the thread."},{"id":"g4","answer":"`envwrap` wraps a callable so that environment variables prefixed with the app name (e.g. `TQDM_`) override parameter defaults: it matches `TQDM_<PARAM>` to the function's parameters, infers the target type from type annotations or from the default value's type, and for union hints tries each type in turn until a cast succeeds; the override is applied by returning a `functools.partial`/`partialmethod` [tqdm/utils.py:34-76]. Examples include `TQDM_MININTERVAL` [tqdm/utils.py:34-76] and the messaging credentials `TQDM_SLACK_TOKEN`/`TQDM_SLACK_CHANNEL`, `TQDM_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`/`TQDM_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`, `TQDM_DISCORD_TOKEN`/`TQDM_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID`, which `tqdm.contrib.bells` also uses to auto-select a backend. Pitfalls: the variable name must correspond to a real parameter; casting depends on usable annotations/defaults; and if the standalone `envwrap` package is installed, tqdm will use it instead, adding config-file support [tqdm/utils.py:79-82]."},{"id":"g5","answer":"The documentation given doesn't answer this — it never describes argument validation in `tqdm.__init__` or any error raised for unknown keywords. The only related item is on the CLI side: options that exist on `tqdm.std.tqdm` but aren't supported by the command line must be listed in `tqdm.cli.UNSUPPORTED_OPTS` [CONTRIBUTING.md:63-64]."},{"id":"g6","answer":"`DisableOnWriteError` is an `ObjectWrapper` around the output stream that intercepts write/flush failures: it catches `OSError` (specifically `errno 5`) and `ValueError` (stream closed) and then disables the associated `tqdm` instance by setting its `miniters` to `inf` [tqdm/utils.py:166-204]. User-visible effect: instead of the program crashing with an I/O error when the output stream dies (e.g. a closed pipe/terminal), the progress bar simply stops refreshing and the surrounding loop keeps running."},{"id":"g7","answer":"The documentation doesn't specify those conditions. It describes `format_meter` as assembling `l_bar` (description + percentage), `bar` (rendered by `Bar.__format__`) and `r_bar` (counts, timing, rate) [tqdm/std.py:465-661], [tqdm/std.py:596-603], and notes that bar width comes from `ncols`/`dynamic_ncols` and that `bar_format` can override the layout — but it never states when the bar and ETA are dropped in favour of a counter-only display despite a `total` being supplied."}]}
